title: Locally finite supported divisors and their normalized Cartier pullback
statement: Let $X$ be an algebraic space and use its codimension-one point classes and Cartier quotient-sheaf sections [def-sfb-space-divisors], with the point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For a prime class $z$, put $|z|=\overline{\{z\}}$. Given a subset $W\subseteq|X|$, the group $\operatorname{Div}_{X\setminus W}(X)$ consists of coefficient functions $d:\operatorname{PrimeDiv}(X)\to\mathbf Z$ such that the family with term $|z|$ when $d(z)\ne0$ and empty term otherwise is locally finite, and every nonzero term is disjoint from $W$. Zero, sums and negatives satisfy these conditions; thus this is the indicated additive subgroup of all coefficient functions, not only finite sums. For a represented scheme $T$ and an open $V\subseteq T$, write $|V|$ for its image in represented point classes using the existing Yoneda embedding [def-sfb-smooth-integral-group-space]. A Cartier section $C$ has coefficient family $d$ if every local affine etale fractional equation of $C$ has the prescribed normalized DVR orders at every codimension-one chart point, using the existing chart orders [def-sfb-space-divisor-operations]. For a flat map $p:X\to Y$, say $e$ is the Cartier pullback of $d$ when there exist Cartier sections with those coefficient families and the second is the actual flat pullback of the first, with the existing local-equation normalization. This relation allows etale pullback to split a prime into several primes.
